status: DRAFT v2 shaped plan by akiendell_cc_0, 2026-11-14, for akienasus to cast. Not built. v2 measures D2 over every proof and REFINES it: the file-level reach read had false positives and missed known positives, so the scope rule below replaces it. See measured.
title: a proof that patches a name the judge it asks reads in another process is refused, naming the patched target
intention: proof_coverage reds a proof file that (1) replaces a module attribute in its own process (patch('pkg.mod.attr'), patch.object(mod, 'attr'), monkeypatch.setattr(mod, 'attr'), or `mod.attr = ...`) AND (2) asks a named judge through inspect_wire (ask('<judge>', ...)), AND (3) the patched (module, attribute) is READ by code the named judge reaches. The red names the proof, the patched target, the judge and the chain from the judge to the module that reads it. A patch whose module the judge never reaches is not red.
why: Three cases measured 2026-11-14, one class: the patch is made in the asking process and the judge that reads the name runs in CodeMother's. (1) corrosion: test_corrosion_sieve tooth 2 patched citation.ruling_covers_path and called ask('constraint_enforcement_holds'); the answerer read the real decisions/ store and the finding fired (149b, commit 2b8400868). (2) 3e08102ef35a (akiendelllinux's): test_the_stones_are_pushed, test_transitions and test_entry_gate_jurisdiction patched _TICKETS while the judge read tickets_root in the answerer (8627334b2). (3) d3248e7cb2fd: c015's tooth 3 substituted crossings.ROOTS and called a judge that now runs in CodeMother (17d570c10390). Each time the proof went red long after the change that moved the judge, and was found by hand.
traces_to: Law 4 (a defect class found three times by hand needs an instrument), Law 3 (the tooth must show the patch is answer-side, not assume it), and memory broad-tooth-manufactures-coverage: a tooth that reds on anything near the property mints false reds.

clauses.claim: a fixture proof that patches citation-style name X and calls ask('<judge>') where the judge's reach reads X is reported, naming the proof, X, the judge and the reach chain
a fixture proof that patches a name in a module the named judge does not reach, patches iw.ask itself, or patches a module it calls in-process is NOT reported (the asker-side negatives)

over the live corpus, before their fixes, the tooth reports corrosion tooth 2, test_transitions, test_entry_gate_jurisdiction, test_the_stones_are_pushed and the d3248 tooth (the five known positives) and none of the seven measured asker-side negatives; every unresolved alias is listed, and the count of hits is asserted as an invariant of the known five, never as a total

decisions.text: D1: the scan lives in cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py, which already parses proofs with ast, NOT in build_inspector/inspector.py (the move chain's collision set). It reads: the patch sites of a proof (the four spellings above, by ast, resolving the dotted module string or the imported name), the judges the proof asks (the first string argument of ask(...) or an ask-lambda alias), and the judge's module from codemother's INSPECT_JUDGES table (cairn/devices/codemother/shim.py:119, read by ast, never imported: RULE 1).

D2 (v2): ANSWER-SIDE AND IN-SCOPE ARE BOTH SHOWN. A patch is flagged only when ALL hold: (a) PATCH SCOPE: the patch is live across an ask-capable call, that is, the call sits in the `with patch(...)` body, or after a `mod.attr = v` assignment in the same function, until the function ends; a patch with no ask-capable call in its scope is silent (this removed the two false positives of the file-level read); (b) ASK-CAPABLE CALL: a literal ask('<judge>') with a judge in INSPECT_JUDGES, a name bound to a lambda or def that asks one (corrosion's `constraint_enforcement_holds = lambda ...: ask(...)`), or a call into cairn/tools/base/transitions.py whose function transitively reaches _judge/_ask_inspector (30 of its functions do: emit, inspect_entry, inspect_proof_named, set_phase and the like, computed by an in-module ast call graph), and, ONE LEVEL, a helper function of the proof itself whose body makes such a call (d3248's `_refused` and `_cross`); (c) ANSWER-SIDE: the patched module is in import_sieve.reaches of the judge's module (for transitions calls, of build_inspector.inspector, the module the lanes ask) AND a reached file reads the attribute name (an ast Name or Attribute load); (d) ALIAS RESOLUTION: `patch.object(X, ...)`, `setattr(X, ...)` and `X.attr = v` resolve X through the proof's own imports; an X that cannot be resolved is LISTED in the output as unresolved, never silently dropped. PLATFORM NOTE: import_sieve.module_name splits on os.sep while the graph keys use '/', so on Windows reaches() returns an empty closure for every start (measured 2026-11-14: 0 hits until the scan used its own splitter). This tooth must use '/' and the build must add a Windows-safe tooth for import_sieve (a one-line fix in a tool, its own ticket).

D3: OUT OF SCOPE, stated so it is not lost: environment patches (patch.dict(os.environ), monkeypatch.setenv) are not module attributes and are CORRECT when made before the launch (the child copies the caller's environment at spawn, scratch.home_env); a dynamic name built at run time, and a judge named by a variable, are invisible to the ast read and pass silently. A proof opts a deliberate case out with a comment naming its ruling, never a skip.
D4: one proof, one tooth per clause, over scratch fixture proofs; clause 3 reads the live corpus and asserts the invariant (the measured positives red, the negatives silent), never a count.

out: fixing the three positives (their own tickets)

measured.saw: POSITIVES (3, answer-side patch measured by reading the judge's reach): (1) cairn/machines/corrosion/proofs/test_corrosion_sieve.py tooth 2: patched cairn.machines.corrosion.citation.ruling_covers_path, asked 'constraint_enforcement_holds', whose reach reads citation.ruling_covers_path; the recorded Dell validation shows the answerer's finding. (2) 3e08102ef35a: test_the_stones_are_pushed, test_transitions, test_entry_gate_jurisdiction (the _TICKETS patch, per akiendelllinux; not re-read here). (3) d3248e7cb2fd: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_dead_proof_name_is_refused_at_proveme.py tooth 3 patched crossings.ROOTS and asked a judge (crossing_proof_named) whose body reads crossings.proven_by_since_buildme; commit 850d9d327 moved the judge over the wire. NEGATIVES (7, asker-side, from the static census): test_the_domain_answers_for_its_migration (patches m.store, calls the proxy handler in-process; its 'ask' is a local helper), test_the_crossing_asks_the_inspector_over_the_bus (patches iw.ask itself, the seam), test_the_ticket_is_three_files (patch(m, '_TICKETS') on probe modules it calls in-process; its one ask is 'buildme_rides_the_sorted' with tickets_root passed as an argument), test_resolve_verb and test_bus_infer (patch host.ollama_resolver around the in-process handler), test_the_verbs_exit_nonzero_on_a_failed_drain (replaces the seam live._ask_codemother with a fake), test_clearance (a fake's own ask method). NOT a case, left out on the orchestrator's correction: the 0c2c draining fake, a signature mismatch. A static grep of patch+ask in the same file found 8 files and a naive 'patch and ask in one file' tooth would have reported 4 of the 7 negatives: that is the false red this design (D2) exists to avoid.
measured.how: scratchpad census over '*/proofs/*.py' for patch(/monkeypatch/setattr beside ask(/inspect_wire, then reading each file's calls; INSPECT_JUDGES at codemother/shim.py:119

measured.saw: D2 MEASURED over every proof in the cairn repo at d41cdc76c and at main f5f9258a3 (identical results; the commons repo has no proofs): 37 judges read from INSPECT_JUDGES (the table is a dict comprehension spread, `**{name: _INSPECTOR for name in (...)}`, so a plain ast read of the dict keys finds 1, not 37: the build must handle the spread). FIRST READ, file-level reach with no scope rule: 21 proofs have a patch site and an asked judge; 5 hit files / 71 sites (test_corrosion_sieve, test_rehearsal, test_the_rehearsal_lane_is_retired, test_the_ticket_is_three_files, test_transitions). Hand classification: FALSE positives 2: test_the_ticket_is_three_files (its patch is an in-process set_phase call; the one ask is in a different function) and the `citation._CAIRN_ROOT` patch in corrosion's worktree tooth (a direct in-process call). MISSED known positives 3 (recall 2 of 5 file-level): test_the_stones_are_pushed and test_entry_gate_jurisdiction (the judge is asked through transitions.inspect_*, not a literal ask('...')) and the d3248 tooth (asked through the proof's own helper `_refused`). SECOND READ, the refined D2 above (scope + ask-capable calls through transitions' call graph, 30 ask-capable functions): 580 patch scopes examined, 83 hit sites in 9 files: corrosion tooth 2 (4 sites; TRUE, a known positive), test_transitions (38; TRUE, 3e08's), test_entry_gate_jurisdiction (6; TRUE, 3e08's), and SIX NEW files not in tonight's three cases: test_clearance (3), test_buildme_rides_the_outline_check (2), test_the_crossing_compares_what_the_inspector_found (2; its comment calls ticket_file._TICKETS 'the one patch point'), test_the_crossing_stands_on_a_certificate (2), test_rehearsal (2) and test_the_rehearsal_lane_is_retired (2). Each of the six patches a name in the asker around calls whose judges read it in the answerer, so the PATTERN is true; whether each is a live RED is not known: I read five of the six by hand (outline_check, compares_found, certificate, rehearsal x2: all patch `ticket_file._TICKETS` around transitions.inspect_*/T.emit) and not test_clearance; none is among akienasus's known reds, so the assertion may not depend on the patched value (a LATENT defect). FALSE positives after the refinement: 0 of the 5 hand-read new files and 0 of the 3 known; test_clearance unread (so the count is 0 known, 1 unread). Still MISSED by the refined read: test_the_stones_are_pushed and the d3248 tooth (their ask goes through a helper two levels down or a launch-lambda; the helper rule above is the fix, not yet re-measured). So: recall on the five known positives is 3 of 5, false 0 of the hand-read: D2 above adds the one-level helper rule for the two misses; the build must re-measure and make clause 3 pass before the tooth is wired.
measured.how: scratchpad reach_scan.py (file level) and reach_scan2.py (scope + ask-capable calls), both throwaway, run over both repos' proofs; import_sieve.reaches with a '/' module_name; hand reading of the contexts

unmeasured: whether the six new files are live reds (a Linux walk would say); the one-level helper rule's effect on the two misses; test_clearance's patch scope by hand; the reach read is exact by import hops and does not see a lazy import inside a function that the graph does record (imports_in walks the whole file, so it does)
land_order: independent of the move chain (D1 keeps it out of inspector.py); cast it after the three positives' fixes land, so clause 3's live read finds them fixed or still red as the clause is worded.
new_finding_for_a_ticket: import_sieve.module_name splits on os.sep, the graph keys use '/', so reaches() is silently empty on Windows: every sieve built on it (fire_path_unreachable, the reach sieves) reads green on Windows by vacuity. A separate small ticket; the fix is `rel_path.split('/')` (keys are already '/'-normalised by import_graph).
